svg.title: Replace iw in the integrand of (BC2) by arbitrary z ∈U. The integral is holomorphic on U. To justify this, regard the integrand as a continuous function on the compact support. Its dependence on z is holomorphic at every point, and it is jointly continuous; locally the Cauchy formula is uniform on that compact set. Integration is a bounded linear functional on the continuous-function space and therefore preserves holomorphy. Equation (BC2) makes this holomorphic integral vanish at imaginary parameters accumulating at zero. The identity theorem on the connected set U makes it vanish at z = 1.
